assessment: All four final lesson visuals are necessary and non-duplicative. The first proves a sample-equivalence counterexample, the first sequence makes spectral replication and overlap spatial, the second sequence makes ideal interpolation an accumulating global sum, and the final comparison separates ideal impulse reconstruction from a realizable zero-order-hold chain. All are course-owned mathematical explanations assembled from exact lesson data, so no photograph, scan, or authenticity-bearing sourced image is appropriate.
scope_guardrail: Use the course CTFT convention X_c(j Omega), engineering j, f=Omega/(2 pi) in hertz, f_s=1/T_s, and omega=Omega T_s=2 pi f/f_s modulo 2 pi in radians/sample. Sampling produces X_s(j Omega)=(1/T_s) sum_k X_c(j(Omega-k Omega_s)); in hertz this is X_s(f)=f_s sum_k X_c(f-k f_s). Strict universal separation is f_s>2B; do not depict equality as safe. Define sinc(u)=sin(pi u)/(pi u), sinc(0)=1, with dimensionless u=(t-nT_s)/T_s. Unit interpolation-kernel height is not the ideal reconstruction filter gain T_s. An anti-alias filter precedes sampling; an output reconstruction/anti-image filter suppresses DAC images but cannot reverse prior aliasing.

resolved_evidence_constraints: The sinusoid comparison is explicitly for zero-phase real cosines: +700 Hz maps to +1.4 pi, represented as -0.6 pi radians/sample, and cosine's conjugate pair makes its six samples equal to the +300 Hz cosine. It does not claim the two positive-frequency complex exponentials are identical.

The replica sequence uses the lesson's exact support B=400 Hz and its exact separated and aliased cases f_s=1000 Hz and f_s=700 Hz; an intermediate f_s=900 Hz frame supplies the requested shrinking positive guard.

To keep replica heights comparable while f_s changes, the plotted ordinate is T_s X_s(f)=sum_k X_c(f-kf_s). Every frame also states the physical relation X_s(f)=f_s times the plotted normalized sum and updates 1/T_s=f_s, so the required sampling scale is not lost or falsely held constant.
Nonoverlap is labeled by the full nearest-support gap f_s-2B. The per-side Nyquist clearance used by the demo is (f_s-2B)/2; the sequence never conflates the two.

The sequence moves from f_s=900 Hz, where the support gap is +100 Hz, directly to f_s=700 Hz, where each nearest neighbor overlaps the central support over 100 Hz. It does not show f_s=800 Hz equality as a safe state.

The sinc sequence freezes an exact reference waveform x_c(t)=sinc((t/T_s-1/2)/2), whose bandwidth is f_s/4. Its five displayed samples are exact values of that waveform, and the black line is always the running partial sum rather than an invented interpolation curve.

The five-kernel sum is labeled a local partial sum. In frame 4 a dashed exact reference reminds the learner that the theorem uses every integer sample; the visual does not imply that five samples reconstruct an arbitrary bandlimited signal.

Every interpolation kernel is x[n] sinc((t-nT_s)/T_s), has value x[n] at its own stem and exact zero contribution at every other integer sample, and is separate from the gain-T_s brick-wall filter in the reconstruction comparison.

The ideal-versus-hold comparison includes the complete zero-order-hold phase factor e^(-j Omega T_s/2), the relative droop 2/pi at f_s/2, the -3.922 dB value, and the first magnitude null at f_s. It depicts residual image lobes around f_s rather than incorrectly placing nonzero energy at the exact hold null.

The ideal branch assumes a strictly interior baseband and uses gain T_s for |Omega|<pi/T_s. Its cutoff is a mathematical selector, not a realizable transition response and not a claim that the Nyquist endpoint is universally recoverable.
The practical output lowpass is named reconstruction/anti-image filtering, not anti-alias filtering; no branch suggests post-sampling filtering can recover analog provenance after overlap.
house_style_adjustments: The replica comment requests red overlap shading, but the house palette permits only amber, blue, green, and currentColor. Use cross-hatched amber plus a heavy currentColor boundary and the text label OVERLAP; meaning must not depend on hue.

The configured course key image is figures/sampling-replicas.svg while the lesson embeds the replica-overlap sequence. Export sampling-replicas.svg as a byte-identical duplicate of replica-overlap-4.svg for metadata/card use; it is a derivative asset, not a fifth instructional figure.

The source citations in the brief are conceptual inspirations only. Recreate every curve, spectrum, and chain from the frozen equations and values; do not trace Oppenheim, Lyons, MIT, or Orfanidis artwork and do not add a credits entry.

figures.pedagogical_necessity: The prose lists hold droop and images, but the side-by-side chain is what prevents learners from merging ideal interpolation, DAC holding, droop compensation, and analog image suppression into one imaginary filter.
figures.tier_reason: The comparison requires two aligned chains, multiple typeset response formulas, miniature time and frequency plots, and a mobile stack. A hook-free component with KaTeX and inline SVG is the correct tier.
figures.source_status: house component derived from the exact ideal-reconstruction and zero-order-hold equations; Orfanidis and Oppenheim are conceptual references only, with no source image and no credit entry
figures.embed: <Figure name="IdealVsHoldReconstruction" alt="Paired chains start from identical samples: an ideal impulse converter and gain-T-s brick-wall lowpass remove spectral images, while a zero-order hold creates a staircase, a half-sample delay, two-over-pi droop at half the sample rate, and residual image lobes for an analog reconstruction lowpass to suppress." caption="Practical reconstruction suppresses spectral images and budgets hold droop, transition width, and delay rather than implementing an infinite sinc exactly." />
figures.teaching_claim: Ideal impulse reconstruction selects one strictly separated baseband with gain T_s, whereas a zero-order hold multiplies all replicas by a delayed sinc response, producing passband droop and attenuated but residual image lobes that require an analog reconstruction filter.

exact_data.common_input: the same discrete samples x[n] at period T_s
exact_data.sampled_spectrum: X_s(j Omega)=(1/T_s) sum_k X_c(j(Omega-k Omega_s)), Omega_s=2pi/T_s
exact_data.ideal_response: H_r(j Omega)=T_s for |Omega|<pi/T_s and 0 for |Omega|>pi/T_s; the signal support is assumed strictly interior, so no endpoint claim is made
exact_data.ideal_impulse_response: h_r(t)=sinc(t/T_s) under the normalized sinc convention
exact_data.zoh_frequency_response: H_0(j Omega)=T_s e^(-j Omega T_s/2) [sin(Omega T_s/2)/(Omega T_s/2)]
exact_data.zoh_normalized_sinc_form: H_0(j Omega)=T_s e^(-j Omega T_s/2) sinc(Omega T_s/(2pi))
exact_data.delay: linear phase -Omega T_s/2 corresponds to T_s/2 delay
exact_data.image_qualification: The hold has zeros at exact multiples of f_s, but nonzero lobes around those centers leave residual images. The analog reconstruction/anti-image lowpass suppresses those lobes and has finite ripple, transition width, attenuation, and delay.

figures.composition: Use a shared top strip containing identical sample stems, then two equal-width comparison cards. The ideal card flows through 'impulse DAC' to a blue gain-T_s brick-wall response and a smooth bandlimited output; its spectrum inset shows a flat retained baseband and removed nearest images. The practical card flows through an amber zero-order hold to a staircase, the full delayed-sinc H_0 formula, and an analog reconstruction LPF; its magnitude inset uses a solid amber sinc envelope with direct points at 0, f_s/2, and f_s and dashed residual image lobes around f_s. Align corresponding stages and add a bottom ledger with gain, passband, phase/delay, and images rows. On mobile, stack complete ideal and hold cards beneath the shared input rather than interleaving stages.
required_labels: H_0(jOmega)=T_s e^{-jOmega T_s/2} sin(Omega T_s/2)/(Omega T_s/2)
